title: Testing Frameworks and Migration Tooling
bodyMarkdown:
# Testing Frameworks and Migration Tooling

Architects advise teams on **how to validate** systems before and during deployment, and on **which tool moves which workload** during a cloud migration.

## The testing pyramid

Balance test types by speed, cost, and quantity:

- **Unit tests** (base): many, fast (seconds), isolate one function/class with mocks. Run on every commit for the quickest regression feedback.
- **Integration tests** (middle): verify components working together, for example a service plus its database. Local **Cloud Emulators** make these fast and free (see module 5).
- **End-to-end / system tests** (top): few, slow, exercise the full deployed stack. Reserve for critical paths.

## Load, stress, and soak testing

These validate **non-functional** behavior:

- **Load testing**: confirm the system handles expected (and N-times-expected) concurrent traffic within latency targets.
- **Stress testing**: push beyond limits to find the breaking point and observe failure modes.
- **Soak testing**: sustained load over time to surface leaks and degradation.

Common tools: **Locust**, **k6**, and **Apache JMeter** generate concurrent virtual users. Run them from infrastructure close to the system (for example a GKE job or a fleet of VMs) and watch Cloud Monitoring during the run.

## Migration tooling decision guide

Matching workload to tool is a high-yield exam skill:

| Workload to migrate | Tool |
|---|---|
| On-prem / AWS / Azure VMs to Compute Engine | **Migrate to Virtual Machines (M2VM)** |
| Databases (MySQL, PostgreSQL, Oracle, SQL Server) to Cloud SQL / AlloyDB | **Database Migration Service (DMS)** |
| Object/file data into Cloud Storage (online) | **Storage Transfer Service** |
| Very large offline data transfer | **Transfer Appliance** |
| Scheduled loads into BigQuery (SaaS, other warehouses) | **BigQuery Data Transfer Service** |
| Containerizing existing apps onto GKE | **Migrate to Containers** |

### Key distinctions

- **M2VM** replicates disks in the background, supports **test clones** for validation, and does a final low-downtime cutover. It is for whole VMs, not databases.
- **DMS** supports continuous replication for **minimal-downtime** database cutover, including heterogeneous migrations.
- **Storage Transfer Service** moves files/objects, never live databases.

## The 7 Rs framing

Migrations are often categorized as Rehost (lift-and-shift, use M2VM), Replatform (minor changes), Refactor (re-architect), Repurchase, Retire, Retain, and Relocate. Match the tool to the strategy: rehost leans on M2VM; database modernization leans on DMS.

## Architect guidance

- Put most automated tests at the unit level; keep e2e tests few and focused.
- Treat load testing as a **pre-launch gate** for any high-traffic event.
- Pick migration tools by workload type, not familiarity; databases use DMS, VMs use M2VM, files use Storage Transfer Service.
- Always validate with test clones / dry runs before cutover, and plan rollback.
